title: aawc-world-heavyweight
label: Dr. Silver

won.source: The card's own commentary and President Schmid's on-camera account of a triangle match "a few weeks ago" before 25 October 1996.

how: Won a triangle match for the AAWC World Heavyweight title against champion Marcus Price and "Superstar" Scotty Michaels, weeks before Oktoberfest '96.
note: Still champion at the surviving record's own last word — Dr. Silver carries the belt through the whole of Oktoberfest '96 (Night 1).

title: aawc-world-heavyweight
label: "Superstar" Scotty Michaels

won.source: The Prodigy Wrestling BB's own FW Central league register of 9 July 1997 bills him "newly crowned AAWC World Heavyweight champion" (promotions/prodigy/archive/fw-central-league-info-1997-07-09.html).

lost.source: The board's own FW Central headlines of 22 July 1997: "in just the last two days, the AAWC World Title changed hands once again at World War Games 3. Former AAWC World Champ Steve Masters took the title from Scotty Michaels in a special stipulation added during the match" (promotions/prodigy/archive/fw-central-headlines-1997-07-22.html).

how: The record does not say how Michaels won the title.
note: The same headline asks whether Michaels can "regain and begin his third title reign in the last two months" — the record therefore carries two Michaels reigns inside that window and dates only this one. The earlier is not registered separately, because nothing held distinguishes its own start or end.

title: aawc-world-heavyweight
label: Steve Masters

won.source: The Prodigy Wrestling BB's own FW Central headlines of 22 July 1997, reporting a change "in just the last two days" at World War Games 3 (promotions/prodigy/archive/fw-central-headlines-1997-07-22.html); the board's own Unified Championship rankings of the same date list "Steve Masters -- AAWC World Champion" (promotions/prodigy/archive/unified-championship-rankings-1997-07-22.html).

how: Took the AAWC World Heavyweight title from Scotty Michaels at World War Games 3, in Wembley Stadium, on a stipulation added during the match.
note: Billed as a FORMER AAWC World Champion when he won it, so at least one earlier Masters reign existed that the record neither dates nor describes. He is still champion at the last word anywhere held, 22 July 1997.

title: aawc-world-heavyweight
label: Hot Shot

won.source: No record of how or when this reign began survives.

how: The record does not say how Hot Shot won the title.

end.source: The CSWA's own Unified World Heavyweight Championship history, dating the IRONMAN of CHAMPIONS at LAST CALL II to 24 October 1993.

note: The earliest AAWC championship fact anywhere in the held record. the CSWA's own Unified World Heavyweight Championship history (promotions/cswa/archive/unified-world-heavyweight-championship-history-1997.html) records that "AAWC World Champion Hot Shot" took part in the IRONMAN of CHAMPIONS at the CSWA's LAST CALL II on 24 October 1993, in the finals of which Hornet defeated Joey Melton, "merging the IWCCW World, AAWC World, and the ten-title CSWA Unified Championship." The reign is recorded as ending with that merge because the title itself was merged; the record does not say what became of Hot Shot's own hold on it. The AAWC bills an AAWC World Heavyweight Championship again on its own card of 25 October 1996, three years later, and nothing held explains how the belt came back.

title: aawc-world-heavyweight
label: Marcus Price

won.source: No record of how or when this reign began survives; the card's own commentary states only that Price had won the title and defended it immediately.

lost.source: The card's own commentary and President Schmid's on-camera statement place the loss "a few weeks ago" before 25 October 1996.

how: The record does not say how Price won the title.
note: Lost in a triangle match against Dr. Silver and "Superstar" Scotty Michaels, with Price's own finisher, the Fashion Statement, suspended by the AAWC offices pending an investigation into a protest Silver had filed.

title: aawc-united-states-heavyweight
label: Dr. Silver

won.source: The card's own commentary: Dr. Silver "outsmarted Price two years ago to beat him for the very same AAWC United States title" (the fed's own Oktoberfest '96 (Night 1) card of 25 October 1996 (promotions/nfw/archive/news-1996-10-25-aawc-oktoberfest-96-night-1.html)).

how: Beat Marcus Price for the AAWC United States Heavyweight title, about two years before Oktoberfest '96.
note: How long Silver held it, and to whom he lost it, is not in the surviving record; by October 1996 he is carrying the AAWC World Heavyweight title instead.

title: aawc-united-states-heavyweight
label: Marcus Price

won.source: The card's own commentary: "newly crowned United States champion", who won the belt in Pittsburgh the week before Oktoberfest '96.

how: Won the AAWC United States Heavyweight title in Pittsburgh, the week before Oktoberfest '96.
note: Defended against Devastating Mike Randalls on the first night of Oktoberfest '96; the surviving copy of that card ends mid-count, so the record does not say whether the reign survived it. The Pittsburgh show on which it was won is not held.

title: aawc-united-states-heavyweight
label: Marcus Price

won.source: No record of how or when this reign began survives.

lost.source: The card's own commentary, dating the loss two years before 25 October 1996: Dr. Silver "outsmarted Price two years ago to beat him for the very same AAWC United States title" (the fed's own Oktoberfest '96 (Night 1) card of 25 October 1996 (promotions/nfw/archive/news-1996-10-25-aawc-oktoberfest-96-night-1.html)).

how: The record does not say how Price won the title.
note: The fed's own commentary reaches back to this reign to explain the 1996 rematch; it dates it only by the phrase "two years ago."

title: aawc-united-states-heavyweight
label: Devastating Mike Randalls

won.source: No record of how or when this reign began survives.

lost.source: No record of how or when this reign ended survives.

how: The record does not say how Randalls won the title.
note: Attested only as a fact about the man: the card's own play-by-play bills Randalls, challenging for the belt on 25 October 1996, as "a former AAWC United States Heavyweight champion in his own right" (the fed's own Oktoberfest '96 (Night 1) card of 25 October 1996 (promotions/nfw/archive/news-1996-10-25-aawc-oktoberfest-96-night-1.html)). The record gives it no date and does not place it against the other recorded reigns on this belt; its position in the lineage here follows the file, not the source.

title: aawc-united-states-heavyweight
label: Anarky

won.source: No record of how or when this reign began survives.

how: The record does not say how Anarky won the title.
note: Champion on 9 July 1997, booked to defend "his US title in a rematch with Mike Chain" at World War Games 3 (promotions/prodigy/archive/fw-central-league-info-1997-07-09.html), and listed as "Anarky -- AAWC US Champion" in the board's own Unified Championship rankings of 22 July 1997 (promotions/prodigy/archive/unified-championship-rankings-1997-07-22.html). Whether he kept it at World War Games 3 is not recorded.

title: aawc-television
label: "Primetime" Xavier Virile
how: Won a triangle match for the AAWC Television title at Oktoberfest '96 (Night 1) in the New Orleans SuperDome. Bloodhunt tagged himself in as champion Lex Taylor hit the Lex Plex, put Taylor down with the Headshot, tagged Virile's arm and rolled him on top for the count.
note: Dr. Silver took the belt from the referee and handed it to Virile himself; the fed's own commentary reads the whole match as a setup running back to Virile's first night in the AAWC.

title: aawc-television
label: "Lethal" Lex Taylor

won.source: No record of how or when this reign began survives; the card's own commentary describes only a long hold on the belt.

lost.source: The next reign's own won date, on the fed's own Oktoberfest '96 (Night 1) card.

how: The record does not say how Taylor won the title.
note: The card's own commentary records that this hold on the belt was "briefly interrupted at one point by Big Mack" and that Taylor "came right back and regained the title in a tag team rematch" — an earlier stretch of the lineage the surviving record neither dates nor sequences, recorded here rather than smoothed into one continuous reign.

title: aawc-television
label: Troy Windham

won.source: No record of how or when this reign began survives.

how: The record does not say how Windham won the title.
note: Champion on 9 July 1997, with "a four corners match for Troy Windham's AAWC Television title" booked at World War Games 3 (promotions/prodigy/archive/fw-central-league-info-1997-07-09.html), and billed on a CSWA card of 15 July 1997 as "currently the Television Champion in the AAWC" (promotions/cswa/archive/cswa-superprimetime-in-san-antonio-1997-07-15.html). Whether he kept it at World War Games 3 is not recorded.

title: aawc-universal-tag-team
label: Battleship & Submarine

won.source: No record of how or when this reign began survives; the card names them only as the reigning champions.

how: The record does not say how the title was won.
note: Billed as THE ARMED FORCES, led by their manager TTL. They retained on the AAWC's own card of 5 August 1995 against ARROGANCE (Joey Melton and Peyton Wright), the referee ruling a double disqualification for the interference of Steven Flair and GUNS (the AAWC's own card of 5 August 1995, AAWC's UNDER NEW OWNERSHIP, served in the CSWA wing (promotions/cswa/archive/aawcs-under-new-ownership-1995-08-05.html)). By 25 October 1996 the belts are on "Showtime" Shawn Matthews and "Flannel Animal" Kurt Taylor; nothing held says when or how they changed hands.

title: aawc-universal-tag-team
label: Shawn Matthews & Kurt Taylor

won.source: No record of how or when this reign began survives; the card names them only as the reigning champions.

how: The record does not say how the title was won.
note: Booked to defend on the second night of Oktoberfest '96 against the Dirty Rotten Scoundrels; that night is not held.

title: aawc-universal-heavyweight
label: "Mr. Magnificent" Tom Adler

won.source: The AAWC's own card of 5 August 1995, whose opening video package replays "Tom Adler celebrating after winning the Universal title" at WrestleFest — the same event at which the fed's presidency was sold (the AAWC's own card of 5 August 1995, AAWC's UNDER NEW OWNERSHIP, served in the CSWA wing (promotions/cswa/archive/aawcs-under-new-ownership-1995-08-05.html)).

lost.source: The CSWA's own Unified World Heavyweight Championship history: "Thanksgiving Weekend 1995... Hornet defends the Unified Championship successfully, getting a pinfall win over 'Mr. Magnificent' Tom Adler, and capturing the AAWC Universal Championship" (the CSWA's own Unified World Heavyweight Championship history (promotions/cswa/archive/unified-world-heavyweight-championship-history-1997.html)).

how: Won the AAWC Universal Heavyweight title at the AAWC's own WrestleFest, beating the fed's own President Robert E. Schmid on the same card.
note: Defended on 5 August 1995 at Cameron Indoor Arena in a steel cage against GUNS, with GUNS' own Enterprises World Heavyweight Championship also at stake: Adler retained the Universal title and took the EN title as well, escaping over the cage while Hornet held GUNS off the arena floor on his shoulders. See this wing's own tier_source. A CSWA retrospective describes WrestleFest '95 differently: "the creation of an AAWC Universal Champion, merging the AAWC World Title with the AAWC Unified Title... The event featured GUNS, Hornet, Doctor Silver and Flic Rair. The first man to defeat his three opponents in consecutive matches would become the new champion" (promotions/cswa/archive/cswa-spotlight-hornet-vs-guns-1998.html), and does not name Adler among the four. The AAWC's own card of 5 August 1995 shows Adler as the reigning Universal Champion and replays his WrestleFest celebration. Both receipts are recorded; neither is picked over the other.

title: aawc-universal-heavyweight
label: Hornet

won.source: The CSWA's own Unified World Heavyweight Championship history, dating the win to Thanksgiving Weekend 1995 (the CSWA's own Unified World Heavyweight Championship history (promotions/cswa/archive/unified-world-heavyweight-championship-history-1997.html)).

how: Beat Tom Adler at Thanksgiving Weekend 1995, retaining the CSWA's own Unified Championship and taking the AAWC Universal title with it.
note: Whether the title was ever defended again, and what became of it, is not in the surviving record; the AAWC's own card of 25 October 1996 names four championships and this is not one of them.

title: aawc-unified
label: Hornet

won.source: A CSWA retrospective's own Hornet/GUNS timeline: "AAWC World War Games / March 1995 / Hornet def. Randalls / For AAWC Unified Title" (promotions/cswa/archive/cswa-spotlight-hornet-vs-guns-1998.html).

how: Beat Mike Randalls for the AAWC Unified Championship at the AAWC's own World War Games in March 1995; the same retrospective records GUNS attacking him immediately afterwards.

end.source: The same retrospective dates WrestleFest '95, at which the AAWC Unified Title was merged with the AAWC World Title to create the AAWC Universal Championship, to May 1995 (promotions/cswa/archive/cswa-spotlight-hornet-vs-guns-1998.html).

note: The title was merged out of existence rather than lost: "the creation of an AAWC Universal Champion, merging the AAWC World Title with the AAWC Unified Title (created from a previous merge of three of the AAWC's lesser titles)." No other holder of this belt is recorded anywhere held.
